headline_marked: Saber denies replacing writers with ChatGPT, [[admits AI for experimental mode]] in Rideshare Stimulator
headline: Saber denies replacing writers with ChatGPT, admits AI for experimental mode in Rideshare Stimulator
summary: Saber's CEO claims the game's story was "written entirely by real people" except for an experimental free-ride mode. This follows a former lead writer's allegation of being replaced by ChatGPT.
details: Saber's CEO Matthew Karch has denied replacing writers with AI for their upcoming "Rideshare Stimulator" game, stating the story was "written entirely by real people." This comes after former lead writer Stella Sacco claimed she was replaced by ChatGPT during development.

Sacco posted on Bluesky that she was the lead writer and Saber replaced her with ChatGPT midway through, also alleging all passenger voices were AI. She suggested a change in direction or a lack of disclosure on Steam.

"Rideshare Stimulator" is described as an immersive driving simulation. Teaser trailers appear to feature AI-generated writing and audio for simulated riders, yet the game's Steam listing currently does not disclose any use of generative AI.

Karch clarified that an "experimental, free-ride mode" will incorporate AI due to the infinite number of passengers. He emphasized Saber's long-standing belief in using AI tools to enhance gameplay and NPC behavior, assuring that none of their 3000+ employees would be replaced by AI.

Sacco countered Karch's statement, arguing that Saber cannot claim human writers created the story while simultaneously admitting AI wrote text. She maintains that if AI-written content is present, she was still replaced as informed in December 2023.

headline_marked: [[CFTC declares market emergency]], orders Kalshi to operate in NY despite $36B lawsuit
headline: CFTC declares market emergency, orders Kalshi to operate in NY despite $36B lawsuit
summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission invoked emergency powers, ordering Kalshi to maintain operations after the New York Attorney General filed a lawsuit seeking to halt event contracts nationwide and over $36 billion in damages.
details: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has exercised its emergency authority, ordering KalshiEX, LLC to continue operating its derivatives market. This action follows Kalshi's notification of a market emergency.

The emergency was triggered by a lawsuit filed by New York Attorney General Letitia James on July 31. The lawsuit seeks a temporary restraining order to stop Kalshi from offering all event contracts nationwide and demands over $36 billion in damages.

The CFTC asserts its mandate under the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) to provide a uniform national market for derivatives. It aims to safeguard market resilience, orderliness, and protect the price discovery process in centralized derivatives markets.

CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig criticized New York's attempt to regulate interstate financial markets under state gaming laws. He stated that Congress intended for derivatives exchanges to be federally regulated, not subject to a "patchwork of state gaming laws."

The Commission has a history of defending its jurisdiction against state enforcement actions, having filed lawsuits against nine states, including New York. It has also submitted amicus briefs in federal appeals courts and a state supreme court to protect its authority.
